title: Two Planes Blow Tires Within Hours at Chicago O'Hare in Third Incident This Week
excerpt: An American Airlines Boeing 737 and a United Airbus A320 both suffered tire failures on landing Monday, with no injuries reported in either case.
body:
• An American Airlines Boeing 737-800 blew two tires upon landing at Chicago O'Hare on Monday afternoon, forcing 180 passengers to be bused to the terminal after the runway was temporarily closed.
  • Three hours later, a United Airlines Airbus A320 arriving from Omaha suffered a burst tire while exiting the same airport's runway, marking the second incident in a single day.
  • No injuries were reported in either incident. The FAA is investigating both, and both aircraft have been removed from service.
  • The incidents follow a separate United Airlines tire blowout at O'Hare just four days earlier, raising questions about runway conditions and maintenance patterns at the nation's busiest airports.

Two passenger aircraft experienced tire blowouts within three hours of each other at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport on Monday, briefly shutting down runways and forcing hundreds of passengers to exit via airstairs and buses.

American Airlines Flight 386

The first incident involved American Airlines Flight 386, a Boeing 737-800 arriving from New York's LaGuardia Airport. Two tires blew out shortly after the aircraft touched down just after 2 p.m. Central time. Fire trucks surrounded the plane on the tarmac.

https://x.com/nypost/status/2089623916302008348

"America 386, you require any assistance? I heard you just blown a tire," an air traffic controller asked, according to audio obtained by NBC News.

"No injuries and no one's panicking. Everyone remains seated," a pilot responded.

The 180 passengers on board were eventually bused to the terminal after the runway was temporarily closed to clear debris. American Airlines said the aircraft was taken out of service for inspection, and the Federal Aviation Administration confirmed it would investigate.

"We thank our team members for their professionalism and we apologize to our customers for their experience."

— American Airlines spokesperson

United Flight 739 Follows Hours Later

At approximately 5:30 p.m. Central time, United Airlines Flight 739, an Airbus A320 arriving from Omaha, suffered a burst main left tire while exiting the runway after landing.

"He's stationary, there's debris over there. Runway 1-0 center is closed, our guy is busy," an air traffic controller reported.

Passengers deplaned via airstairs and were transported to the terminal by bus. United confirmed the tire damage in a statement but provided no further details on the cause.

Authorities said there was no indication the two incidents were connected, noting they occurred at different parts of the airport.

Third Incident in Days

The back-to-back blowouts came just four days after a separate United Airlines flight bound for Phoenix was forced to abort its takeoff at O'Hare after suffering two blown tires. "We saw lots of chunks of tire going down the runway," a pilot said in that incident, according to Live ATC audio. The 161 passengers and six crew were deplaned safely.

Three tire incidents at the same airport within a week is unusual, though aviation experts caution against drawing conclusions without detailed investigations. Tire failures during landing can result from high-speed contact with runway debris, overheated brakes, underinflation, or manufacturing defects.

What Travelers Should Know

O'Hare is one of the busiest airports in the United States and a major hub for both American and United Airlines, handling more than 80 million passengers annually. While tire blowouts are considered relatively low-risk incidents — aircraft are designed to land safely even with multiple tire failures — the clustering of three events in less than a week is likely to draw heightened scrutiny from the FAA.

For passengers, the practical impact is limited to potential delays if runways are temporarily closed for inspection and debris clearance. Both airlines rebooked affected passengers on later flights.
